text: Correctly stated: `le_det` requires `f x₀ ≤ det D²φ(x₀)` when a locally convex C² test function touches `u` from above. This is the subsolution sign for the elliptic Monge–Ampère operator in [Amadori–Brandolini–Trombetti, §2](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/39615#page=3). Convexity of `u` is a separate application hypothesis, as in the [Aleksandrov bridge](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Convex/MongeAmpere/Viscosity.lean#L235); it need not be a structure field. The [convex C² comparison](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Convex/MongeAmpere/Viscosity.lean#L422) passes and identifies both test conditions with the classical equation. Empty domains are harmless, and no finite-dimensional classical interpretation is asserted for the unrestricted predicate outside its consumers’ hypotheses. Roadmap6A.3 has no separately tagged check for this component.
Convex Aleksandrov subsolutions with continuous density satisfy this precise upper-touching condition.
The pair of viscosity conditions specializes to the classical determinant equation for convex C² functions.

Correctly stated: `det_le` imposes `det D²φ(x₀) ≤ f x₀` for locally convex C² tests touching `u` from below. This matches the supersolution inequality for the convex elliptic branch in [Amadori–Brandolini–Trombetti, §2](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/39615#page=3). The [measure comparison theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Convex/MongeAmpere/Viscosity.lean#L311) retains convexity and nonnegative continuous data; the [convex C² equivalence](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Convex/MongeAmpere/Viscosity.lean#L422) also passes. Those hypotheses exclude the earlier strictly concave counterexample to an unrestricted interpretation. The structure deliberately stores the testing condition alone, with no uniqueness or boundary claim. Roadmap6A.3 has no separate tagged check for this component.
Convex Aleksandrov supersolutions with continuous nonnegative density satisfy the lower-touching determinant inequality.
For convex C² functions the combined test conditions are equivalent to the classical equation.

Correctly stated: the definition combines `0 < λ ≤ Λ`, the lower quadratic bound `λ‖ξ‖² ≤ ξᵀAξ`, and the full bilinear bound `|ηᵀAξ| ≤ Λ‖η‖‖ξ‖` at every domain point. These are the real version of the bounded elliptic matrix assumptions in [Pipher, slide7](https://www.icmat.es/congresos/2022/Escorial/slides/Courses/Pipher.pdf#page=7). The second bound controls the skew part as well; symmetry and measurability are not silently assumed. [Identity coefficients](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/Ellipticity/Basic.lean#L830) pass with λ=Λ=1, and the [operator-norm consequence](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/Ellipticity/Basic.lean#L661) passes. On an empty domain the two constant conditions remain. No separately tagged roadmap check accompanies this primitive predicate.
The identity coefficient field satisfies the predicate with exact constants1,1.
The full two-vector bound controls the operator norm, including nonsymmetric coefficients.

Correctly stated: if `Ω′ ⊆ Ω`, every pointwise ellipticity and boundedness inequality already known on `Ω` holds on `Ω′`, with exactly the same λ and Λ. Lean preserves the positive ordered constants and applies the original bounds through the subset map. This is restriction of the [defining inequalities](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/Ellipticity/Basic.lean#L546), consistent with [Pipher’s domainwise bounds](https://www.icmat.es/congresos/2022/Escorial/slides/Courses/Pipher.pdf#page=7). Equality of domains and the empty subset cause no exception; enlarging the domain is not claimed. The native [identity-field calibration](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/Ellipticity/Basic.lean#L830) passes on every domain. No standalone roadmap Check is assigned to this elementary restriction lemma.
Identity coefficients provide a nonvacuous calibration on any restricted domain.

Correctly stated: `bilinearComp` restricts both arguments of the continuous H¹ energy form along the H¹₀ inclusion. Thus the value remains ∫(∇vᵀA∇u+(b·∇u)v+cuv), with the same test/solution order as [Pipher’s weak form, slide8](https://www.icmat.es/congresos/2022/Escorial/slides/Courses/Pipher.pdf#page=8). The essential-boundedness hypothesis on the pointwise bilinear coefficient supplies continuity; coercivity is a separate later hypothesis. [Evaluation on the underlying Sobolev functions](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/EnergyForm/Sobolev.lean#L740) passes. H¹₀ membership supplies the zero boundary condition without requiring a trace theorem. PDE D.16 has no separately tagged restriction check; the [ball Poisson application](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/DirichletProblem.lean#L623) passes.
The restricted bundled form evaluates to the unchanged H¹ energy form on the two subtype inclusions.
The restricted form supports the concrete ball Poisson weak-solution theorem.

Correctly stated: this is the Lax–Milgram solution for `B = energyFormH1L0 hcoeff` and `ℓ(v)=∫fv`. Its H¹₀ result type encodes homogeneous Dirichlet data. Boundedness is supplied by `hcoeff`, and `hcoercive` is an explicit additional assumption, exactly the hypotheses of [Evans§6.2.1, pp297–299](https://math24.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/02/partial-differential-equations-by-evans.pdf#page=303). The [weak identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/DirichletProblem.lean#L295) and [uniqueness characterization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/DirichletProblem.lean#L304) both pass, so the construction has no arbitrary-solution ambiguity. The [ball Poisson check](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/DirichletProblem.lean#L623) passes; the shared roadmap’s smoothness and corrected Newtonian comparison are separately source-present. No smooth boundary or coefficient symmetry is needed by this abstract construction.
The constructed H¹₀ element satisfies every weak test equation.
Every solution of that weak problem equals the constructed element.
Identity coefficients on a ball-contained domain supply an unconditional concrete coercive instance.
The separately scoped smoothness component of the shared PDE criterion is source-present.
The separately scoped Newtonian comparison includes its required harmonic boundary correction.

Correctly stated: the constructed `weakSolutionDirichlet` satisfies `B(u,v)=∫fv` for every H¹₀ test function. Expanding [the weak-solution predicate](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/DirichletProblem.lean#L193) and the restricted form gives exactly that variational equation, the defining conclusion of [Evans’s Lax–Milgram theorem, p298](https://math24.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/02/partial-differential-equations-by-evans.pdf#page=304). The source retains bounded coefficients and coercivity; zero boundary data comes from the H¹₀ result type, not an unstated trace assumption. The [ball Laplacian existence check](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/DirichletProblem.lean#L623) passes, while smoothness and the harmonic-corrected Newtonian comparison are separate source-present components. This lemma claims the weak identity alone, without adding pointwise regularity.
Expands IsWeakSolutionDirichlet to the intended integral equation for all H¹₀ tests.
The bundled restricted form has exactly the raw energy value.
Concrete ball Laplacian instance confirms the weak existence interpretation.
The shared smoothness component is separately available under its own data hypotheses.
The shared Newtonian comparison is available with the explicitly assumed harmonic boundary correction.

Correctly stated: any H¹₀ weak solution with the same coefficients and forcing equals the Lax–Milgram construction. Subtracting the two variational identities and testing with their difference gives `B(w,w)=0`; coercivity forces `w=0`, exactly [Evans’s uniqueness argument, p299](https://math24.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/02/partial-differential-equations-by-evans.pdf#page=305). Equality is equality of Sobolev classes, so no arbitrary representatives are identified pointwise. The assumptions retain boundedness and coercivity, with no symmetry requirement. The [concrete ball existence-and-uniqueness check](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/DirichletProblem.lean#L623) passes. Smoothness and the harmonic-corrected Newtonian comparison remain separately source-present and add no hidden assumptions to this uniqueness statement.
The equality hypothesis is precisely the weak variational equation, not an assumed equality with the constructed solution.
The native Laplacian ball theorem includes uniqueness with the intended boundary condition.
Separate smoothness witness for the shared roadmap criterion.
Separate corrected Newtonian comparison with its explicit boundary hypotheses.

Correct: tensor linearization sends x⊗y to the bounded map f↦f(x)y. The bidual evaluation map supplies f(x), and `smulRight` supplies multiplication by y, so linearity makes this independent of the chosen finite decomposition. This is exactly the operator associated with a tensor in [Ryan, §3.1](https://djvu.online/file/ATNjYmfESxgzE). Seminormed factors and incomplete spaces cause no problem; injectivity is a separate result requiring stronger hypotheses.

Correct: evaluation of the tensor-linearized bilinear map at x⊗y gives f(x)•y, with the functional applied to the left factor. This follows directly from [the construction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Normed/Module/TensorProduct/InjectiveSeminorm.lean#L72). The statement holds for every bounded functional, including zero, and does not assume the two factors are complete or definite.

Correct: pulling the operator-norm seminorm back along `contractStrongDual` gives ε(u)=‖f↦∑f(xᵢ)yᵢ‖. This is [Ryan’s operator formula, §3.1](https://djvu.online/file/ATNjYmfESxgzE). The docstring restricts its scalar-dual supremum identification to ℝ/ℂ, as does `injectiveSeminorm_le_iff_forall_norm_le_one`; it makes no unsupported Hahn–Banach assertion over arbitrary normed fields. Zero and seminorm-degenerate factors remain valid.

Correct: the displayed equality evaluates [the pullback seminorm](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Normed/Module/TensorProduct/InjectiveSeminorm.lean#L97) at u. `normSeminorm.comp` is precisely the norm of the image under `contractStrongDual`, so the natural-language operator-norm description and Lean equality coincide without extra hypotheses.

Correct: the pure-tensor operator is f↦J(x)(f)y, where J is bidual evaluation. Its norm is ‖J(x)‖‖y‖ by [the rank-one operator norm identity](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Operator/Bilinear.lean#L451). The statement deliberately retains ‖J(x)‖ rather than assuming J is isometric over every nontrivially normed field. The zero-factor cases also satisfy the formula.

Correct: [the pure-tensor formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Normed/Module/TensorProduct/InjectiveSeminorm.lean#L114) gives ε(x⊗y)=‖J(x)‖‖y‖, and [the bidual contraction bound](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Module/DoubleDual.lean#L73) gives ‖J(x)‖≤‖x‖. Multiplication preserves this inequality because ‖y‖≥0. Thus the stated upper bound holds in the general field/seminormed setting without claiming equality there.

Correct: membership records a natural number n and two Fin n families whose tensor sum is u and whose sum of norm products is the proposed cost. This represents all finite decompositions, with n=0 allowing the empty decomposition of zero. It is the family used in [Ryan’s projective-norm definition, equation (2.2)](https://djvu.online/file/ATNjYmfESxgzE); no decomposition is selected by the definition.

Correct: every algebraic tensor has a finite pure-tensor decomposition by [TensorProduct.exists_sum_tmul_eq](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Finiteness.lean#L182). Its sum of norm products is consequently an element of [the cost set](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Normed/Module/TensorProduct/ProjectiveSeminorm.lean#L63). No topological completeness is needed. This lemma rules out an empty infimum family for every u, including zero.

Correct: every member of [the cost set](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Normed/Module/TensorProduct/ProjectiveSeminorm.lean#L63) is a finite sum of products of nonnegative real norms. Zero is therefore a lower bound. `BddBelow` asserts existence of such a bound, exactly the property needed for the real conditional infimum; it does not assert positivity for nonzero tensors.

Correct: the displayed finite family is itself a decomposition of its tensor sum, so its cost belongs to [the set being minimized](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Normed/Module/TensorProduct/ProjectiveSeminorm.lean#L63). That set is bounded below by zero; hence its real infimum is no greater than this member. The finite index may be empty, and the conclusion still reads 0≤0.

Correct: the empty decomposition has cost zero and represents the zero tensor, while [nonnegativity of every cost](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Normed/Module/TensorProduct/ProjectiveSeminorm.lean#L74) gives the opposite inequality. Thus the infimum is exactly zero. This establishes the normalization used in the seminorm construction and does not rely on the default value of an empty real infimum.

Correct: appending a decomposition of u to one of v decomposes u+v with cost equal to the sum of their costs. Both cost sets are nonempty and bounded below, so taking their infima gives exactly the displayed subadditivity inequality. The [source argument](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Normed/Module/TensorProduct/ProjectiveSeminorm.lean#L89) uses `Fin.append`; it never assumes an infimum is attained.

Correct: multiplying the left vectors in any decomposition of u by a decomposes a•u and multiplies its cost by ‖a‖. Taking infima yields the stated inequality; the nonnegativity of ‖a‖ justifies transporting the infimum through multiplication. [Nonemptiness](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Normed/Module/TensorProduct/ProjectiveSeminorm.lean#L70) also covers a=0, so no inverse scalar or nonzero-scalar hypothesis is needed.

Correct: the underlying function is the infimum of all finite decomposition costs, exactly [Ryan’s π, equation (2.2)](https://djvu.online/file/ATNjYmfESxgzE). Its cost family is nonempty and bounded below; the supplied zero, sum and scalar bounds bundle it as a seminorm. The declaration claims a seminorm over an arbitrary normed field. Definiteness and the ℝ/ℂ cross-norm identities are proved separately, so seminorm-degenerate factors are intentionally allowed.

Correct: [the seminorm constructor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Normed/Module/TensorProduct/ProjectiveSeminorm.lean#L111) keeps the function u↦inf(costs(u)) as its underlying value. Evaluating it therefore gives exactly this equality. `costs` ranges over all finite decompositions of the same algebraic tensor, with no completion or minimizing decomposition involved.

Correct: linearity of f and subadditivity of p bound p(f(u)) by C times the cost of every finite decomposition of u. Since C≥0, taking the infimum gives p(f(u))≤Cπ(u), using [the actual definition of π](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Normed/Module/TensorProduct/ProjectiveSeminorm.lean#L111). The codomain needs only a module and its stated seminorm, not a separate normed topology. C=0 is valid and no attainment of the infimum is assumed.

Correct: `p ≤ projectiveSeminorm` is the pointwise maximality assertion for seminorms satisfying the stated pure-tensor bound. Taking f to be the identity and C=1 in [the general cost bound](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Normed/Module/TensorProduct/ProjectiveSeminorm.lean#L145) proves exactly p(u)≤π(u) for every u. The hypothesis is only on pure tensors, so it does not assume the conclusion on arbitrary tensor sums.

The simple-root triples generate the split Killing algebra and satisfy the Serre relations, giving the stated surjection with prescribed coroot images, as in [Etingof, Theorem 24.1](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-755-lie-groups-and-lie-algebras-ii-spring-2024/mit18_755_s24_lec_full.pdf#page=130). Since the root-first convention is Aᵢⱼ=αᵢ(hⱼ), [Lean correctly uses Aᵀ](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/Presentation/Serre/Killing.lean#L215).

The [nonsymmetric rank-three Check](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/LieHighestWeight/README.md#L1186) passes through published comparisons: the [rational B₃ base](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/SimplyConnectedRootDatum/Rational.lean#L240) has A₁₂=−2,A₂₁=−1; actual orthogonal matrix generators have [Cartan eigenvalues](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/Orthogonal/TypeB/GeneratorRelations.lean#L194) −1,−2 and opposite negative-generator signs. Their [higher relations](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/Orthogonal/TypeB/SerreRelations.lean#L326) have total adjoint powers 2,3 in both positive and negative systems. These are assembled source checks, not a separately packaged fixture. Later representation examples concern other targets. No local rebuild is claimed.
The actual rational root-system base has the Bourbaki Cartan matrix; at B3 nodes1,2 this gives entries -2 and -1. Source-backed composite check, not a standalone fixture.
Actual orthogonal matrix generators have Cartan eigenvalue A(j,i); at B3 nodes1,2 the two eigenvalues are -1 and -2, detecting the transpose.
Actual negative orthogonal generators have the opposite Cartan eigenvalues, giving +1 and +2 at the B3 terminal pair.
Actual positive matrix generators satisfy the higher Serre relations; the B3 terminal pair has total adjoint powers2 and3 after including the initial bracket.
The negative generators satisfy the same B3 terminal higher exponents2 and3, via the proved signed matrix reindexing.

The rendered `↑ℓ ≠ 0` is a condition in the residue field, as [the source specifies](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/TateModule/PotentialGoodReduction.lean#L402); even in characteristic zero it is substantive. Potential good reduction means good reduction after a finite extension and minimization, while the representation acts on actual compatible ℓ-power torsion points. This is [Silverman VII.7.3](https://www.math.ens.psl.eu/~obenoist/refs/Silverman.pdf).

Additional boundary evidence: the converse uses K(E[ℓ²]) and proves ℓ²≥3 before Serre’s lemma, covering ℓ=2 without incorrectly using its level-two criterion. The forward implication factors through a finite normal extension. [Layer 4](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves/README.md#L851) separates this equivalence from the finite-level good-reduction statement; its 11a1 warning concerns that different claim. No further concrete Check is attached here. Source and current rendered statement inspected; no local compilation claimed.

The source compares finite-support ordered simplex chains with singular homology of the weak realization [through cellular homology](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/SimplicialComplex/Realization/CWComplex/OrderedChainComplex.lean#L181), matching [Hatcher, Theorems 2.27 and 2.35](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=137). The additional orientation evidence is that [cellular incidences](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/SimplicialComplex/Realization/CWComplex/AlternatingIncidence.lean#L411) equal (−1)^jεₙ, where εₙ is a proved unit. Degreewise rescaling gives exactly the alternating deleted-vertex boundary. This works for any ring and infinite complexes; empty complexes and degree zero are included.

The [Layer 11 realization Check](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/GeometricTopology/README.md#L974) passes via the actual [simplex-boundary/sphere homeomorphism](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/SimplicialComplex/Simplex/BoundarySphere.lean#L345). The incidence, unit and chain-component formulas are proved supporting checks. The declaration claims this constructed isomorphism; it does not add naturality or a prescribed generator normalization. Source inspected; no local rebuild claimed.
Actual cellular incidences have the alternating signs up to the single degree-dependent unit.
The orientation factor is invertible, so the degreewise rescaling preserves homology.
The chain comparison has the stated concrete degreewise components.
The native ordered boundary is the alternating sum of deleted-vertex faces, over any ring.
Layer11 realization round-trip: the actual simplex boundary is homeomorphic to the sphere, including an infinite ambient vertex set.

The determinant product is positive exactly when Hirsch’s relative derivative has positive determinant: the derivatives are invertible, so product and quotient have the same sign. Changing charts multiplies the product by a positive square. Thus no global orientation is needed. [Hirsch, Chapter 4, Theorem 6.6](https://math.stanford.edu/~ralph/math215b/Hirsch.pdf#page=127) gives this open-disc isotopy fixing the centre.

[Lean’s witness](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/SmoothIsotopy/DiscTheorem.lean#L68) is a `SmoothIsotopy f g`: jointly smooth, with the specified endpoints and every slice an immersion and topological embedding. The [Euclidean and ball-confined versions](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/SmoothIsotopy/Euclidean.lean#L128) and endpoint formulas pass without sorry, including dimension zero. [GeometricTopology Layer 1](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/GeometricTopology/README.md#L223) uses this prerequisite; its gluing computations concern later connected sums. No ambient extension or compact-support conclusion is asserted. Source inspected; no local compilation claimed.
The self-model specialization uses the same determinant sign and fixes the common centre.
The entire interpolation remains in a ball, permitting legitimate chart inversion.
The bundled isotopy begins at the specified embedding.
The bundled isotopy ends at the specified embedding.
